slides.title: Delegation
slides.subtitle: Vouch for a delegated key with claims that name no User and no Company
slides.notes: Session JWTs are signed with a short-lived delegated key, not with a key from the agent's jwks_uri. A delegation is how a jwks key vouches for that delegated key. This example shows what goes into one, and what stays out.

slides.title: Why a delegation
slides.statement: The keys in `jwks_uri` sign **a key**, never a request, so they never see a **User** or a **Company**.
slides.notes: A delegation identifies the agent and the delegated public key, and expires quickly. It says nothing about the User or the Company. The Session JWT it vouches for carries those, signed by the delegated key.

slides.title: Who takes part
slides.diagram:
flowchart LR M["Model"] subgraph HOST["Your host, trusted"] direction TB H["PAP host
a key per User ID"] -- "resolve subject" --> P[("Pairwise ID store")] H -- "sign the claims" --> S["Reactor signer
a key in jwks_uri"] end subgraph CO["Company"] direction TB A["Company API
verifies delegation, then JWT"] end HOST -- "Session JWT with its delegation" --> CO HOST -. "claim names, lifetime" .-> M
slides.caption: The subject and the keys stay in the host; the model learns which claims exist and how long they last.
slides.notes: Inside your trusted host, the PAP host resolves the user's pairwise User ID for this company from the pairwise ID store, and makes a delegated key for that User ID. The Reactor signer, holding a key from the agent's jwks_uri, signs the delegation without the private key ever leaving it. The compact delegation travels in the header of each Session JWT, and the company verifies it first. Off to the side, the model gets the claim names and the lifetime, never the subject, the jti, the delegation or a key.

slides.title: How it flows

items.title: Resolve
items.detail: The pairwise User ID for this company

items.title: Make a key
items.detail: One delegated P-256 key for that User ID

items.title: Carry
items.detail: In `pap_dlg`, in each Session JWT's header

items.title: Verify
items.detail: The delegation, then the Session JWT

slides.notes: The host resolves the User ID and makes a delegated key for it; a key is never shared by two User IDs. The Reactor signer signs a delegation for the key, with the purpose delegation. Each Session JWT carries it in its pap_dlg header. Before the delegation expires, the signer rotates: a new key and a new delegation. It never signs after expiry.

slides.title: What each claim does

rows.label: iss
values: Names the agent, and where its keys are

rows.label: cnf
values: The key allowed to sign Session JWTs

rows.label: iat, exp
values: Bounds how long a stolen key is useful

rows.label: jti
values: No two delegations look the same

slides.notes: Each claim is there for the company to check the key, and none says who it is for. There is no sub, no aud, no Agent ID. A delegation can't be withdrawn before it expires, so its lifetime limits what a stolen delegated key can do. The subject stays pairwise in the Session JWT: two companies cannot correlate a user by comparing PAP identifiers.

slides.title: How the company checks it
slides.diagram:
flowchart LR S["Signed by the jwks key
its kid names?"] -- "yes" --> U["typ, iss,
at most 24 hours?"] U -- "yes" --> T["Unexpired?"] T -- "yes" --> J["Session JWT signed
by cnf.jwk?"] J -- "yes" --> OK["Check the Session JWT's claims"] S -- "no" --> R["400 invalid_session"] U -- "no" --> R T -- "no" --> R J -- "no" --> R
slides.caption: Every check must pass; one failure is invalid_session.
slides.notes: Read it left to right, as the company does. It fetches the agent's client metadata and jwks_uri, and the delegation must verify with the key its kid names. Its typ must be pap-delegation+jwt, its iss the JWT's client_id, and its lifetime 24 hours at most. It must not have expired. Then the Session JWT must verify with the key in cnf.jwk. A Session JWT signed directly by a jwks key, with no delegation, is refused. A company may cache a verified delegation until it expires. Any failure is 400 with invalid_session.

slides.title: Run it yourself
slides.cta: The Pydantic AI and Agent Runtimes examples sign a real delegation and return only its policy
slides.notes: The small example stops at the delegation's claims: a Reactor plugin contributes a SQLite pairwise store, and the tool reports the claim names, the lifetime, and that no User and no Company are named. The Session lifecycle example sends a Session JWT with its delegation on each request.
